subject: Capital Improvement Plan FY23–FY28
overview: The committee reviewed a presentation from the Collins Center on the city's updated $170.8 million Capital Improvement Plan for fiscal years 2023 through 2028. The plan prioritizes over 200 projects funded through a mix of debt, ARPA funds, and state grants while aiming for a stabilized 3% debt-to-budget ratio.

items.title: Capital Improvement Plan Presentation
items.summary: Sarah Concannon of the Collins Center presented a six-year plan identifying 217 projects totaling $170.8 million across all city departments.

items.title: Asset Management and Assessment Strategy
items.summary: Councilors discussed the necessity of comprehensive asset inventories and architectural facility assessments to quantify total deferred maintenance costs versus current project-based priorities.

items.title: Financial Targets and Funding Sources
items.summary: The strategy targets maintaining general fund debt service at 3% of the net budget while leveraging ARPA funds and free cash for pay-as-you-go projects to minimize interest costs.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Proposal
items.summary: Approved a motion requesting the establishment of a capital stabilization fund to be funded by a fixed percentage of the annual free cash surplus. The proposal aims to institutionalize long-term capital planning and provide consistent funding for infrastructure needs.

items.title: Project Totals and Departmental Breakdown
items.summary: The committee reviewed project distributions, noting significant funding for fire headquarters, high school renovations, and road infrastructure, with 27% of total costs covered by external grants.
